### Prerequisites

In this text, we will practice adding negative numbers. Before practicing, we suggest studying the texts from Chapter 3 of the *First Steps* section of *History Tracers* (<htcite0>), as well as the text that explains the relationship between negative numbers and a path (<htcite1>).

### Sun Tzu's (孙子) 5 factors The numbers in this exercise are negative, so the minus sign is part of each number — do not forget it. To do the exercises, we recommend using Sun Tzu's 5 factors (the same ones from **The art of studying** ()) as follows: - **The law of morale**: Do not stop after a single exercise. To reinforce what you have learned, practice until you feel more comfortable, and spread your practice over more than one day. - **Heaven**: Visualize the negative numbers you are adding with your own body. Every time you add one negative number to another, check whether the magnitude stays within the count of your fingers or goes beyond it, and remember that the result stays on the negative side. Then try to recreate the additions you are doing here in other scenarios, so you realize that the same idea appears everywhere. - **Terrain**: In every addition, squares represent the digits of the magnitudes. The minus sign does not have a square: it is written in its own column, where the ten thousands place would be, and it must be kept in the result. When a column carries 1, its sum has reached 10 or more — beyond the digits 0 to 9 — so extra squares appear outside the group of ten. So, before you start adding two digits, ask yourself: is the second digit at least as large as the complement of the first? If it is, the column will carry 1. Do not forget the signs: a result without the minus sign is a different number. - **The commander**: As the commander of your learning, you should: - Be benevolent with yourself and with people who have not understood the addition of negative numbers yet, and help them learn. - Be honest with yourself, and do not let your confidence underestimate or overestimate the problem ahead of you. - Respect yourself by remembering that there are different ways to understand math. Discover the way that makes you feel comfortable and follow it. At History Tracers, we will do our best to help you find your road. - Use your wisdom to identify your weaknesses, so you can train them and turn them into strengths. - Use your sincerity to see where you need to improve, and do not build barriers because of the difficulties you may find. - **Method and discipline**: Set aside a period of time to train every day, and respect your rest time. ### Practice Exercise Reading about addition helps, but practice is essential for real understanding. Below is an addition of two negative numbers, written vertically, column by column, from the units to the hundreds. Because both numbers are negative, we add their magnitudes — the numbers without their signs — and keep the minus sign in the result. In each column: 1. The light blue squares show the digit of the magnitude already in the column. 2. Use the up button () to add one square and the down button () to remove one square, until the light yellow squares match the digit of the second number in this column. 3. When the count reaches ten squares, those ten are grouped and become the 1 carried to the next order. Before clicking the buttons, look at the complement of the value already in the column: the complement tells you how many squares are still missing to reach ten. Then associate the squares with the result: the group of ten becomes the 1 carried to the next order, and the squares left outside the group are the digit that stays in the column. **Example: (-8) + (-7).** The column already holds 8 light blue squares, and the 7 from the second number is added to them. The complement of 8 to ten is 2, so the first 2 added squares close the group of ten (the 1 carried to the next order), and the remaining 5 squares stay outside the group. Those squares give the digit 5 of the magnitude; since both numbers are negative, the result is -15:
8 + 7 = 15 When you finish the calculation, you will receive a medal () and you can move on to the next problem by clicking the button below:
